sources.title: A multi-level society comprised of one-male and multi-male core units in an African colobine (Colobus angolensis ruwenzorii)
sources.locator: Abstract; Materials and Methods, study population and data collection; Results, core units and non-random associations.
sources.scope: Primary field study of one Rwenzori Angolan colobus band at Lake Nabugabo, Uganda, using observations from August 2017 to July 2018; the studied taxon is the subspecies Colobus angolensis ruwenzorii.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution License, stated in the article copyright statement; the article does not specify a numbered version.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Copyright statement after the article citation; Creative Commons Attribution License.
sources.attribution: Stead SM, Teichroeb JA (2019). A multi-level society comprised of one-male and multi-male core units in an African colobine (Colobus angolensis ruwenzorii). PLoS ONE 14(10):e0217666. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0217666. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: During a year of observations at Lake Nabugabo, the researchers identified 135 individuals in 12 core units ranging from 4 to 23 individuals.
claims.scope: One study band of Colobus angolensis ruwenzorii at one Ugandan site; observations were collected from August 2017 through July 2018.

claims.text: Association analyses found that some core units associated preferentially in two clans, supporting three observed levels of social organization: core unit, clan, and band.
claims.scope: A result from this studied subspecies and band; it is not evidence that all Colobus angolensis populations share the same organization.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
This field study does not establish species-wide social organization, diet, range, abundance, or current conservation status.
